options.content:
One stream of requests; each sample is one request, and its value is the client ID. The synthetic data runs 120 minutes with 1 series per metric. | column | what it is | values | |---|---|---| | time | Time of the sample | One sample every 2 ms (500 per second) | | requests | ID of the client that sent the request | Usual values: Zipf distribution (skew 1) over 100,000 values
Minutes 30 to 70, ramping in and out over 20 minutes: 3% of samples are random values, uniform over the whole numbers 200,000 to 200,002
Minutes 80 to 110, ramping in and out over 5 minutes: 2% of samples are random values, uniform over the whole numbers 300,000 to 300,001
Note: whole numbers; never below 0; each sample's value is stored as the label client_id |

Each query runs twice, once with the exact plan and once with the approximate plan. A rule reads query results and decides an action; exact and approx decide separately, and the dashboard compares their decisions. On the time charts below, shaded areas are the problem periods injected into the synthetic data, and vertical marks are the times when the selected rule decided differently on approx than on exact; a rule that always decides the same has no marks.

**Queries**

| query | PromQL | computed |
|---|---|---|
| top10_clients | `topk(10, sum by (client_id) (count_over_time(requests[5m])))` | every 60 s over the last 300 s |
| top10_clients_1m | `topk(10, sum by (client_id) (count_over_time(requests[1m])))` | every 60 s over the last 60 s |

**Rules**

| rule | queries it uses | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| top_clients | top10_clients | A client is capped while it is in the top 10 list |
| aws_waf | top10_clients | A client among the top 10 over 5 minutes with more than 2,000 requests is limited while it stays over (AWS WAF rate-based rule, the AWS blog's limit) |
| cloud_armor | top10_clients_1m | A client among the top 10 over 1 minute with more than 500 requests is banned for the rest of the interval plus 600 s (Google Cloud Armor default policy's 500 per 60 s; ban_duration_sec ours) |
| fastly | top10_clients_1m | A client among the top 10 over 1 minute above 20 requests per second goes into the penalty box for at least 2 minutes (Fastly; the rate ours, over 1 minute instead of 10 s) |

panels.title: VictoriaMetrics, which keeps every raw sample, vs ASAPQuery-backend planned to keep none: writes, memory, disk and query latency
panels.description: VictoriaMetrics answers are the exact arm, ASAPQuery-backend answers the approx arm. One sender writes both in time order; at each evaluation time it makes the samples written so far visible (a watermark for ASAPQuery-backend, a flush for VictoriaMetrics) and asks the queries due then, one instant query each. Write seconds include the visibility calls. Peak resident bytes and CPU seconds cover the whole process; disk bytes is the data directory at the end, and ASAPQuery-backend keeps everything in memory.

panels.title: Every run and query: plan, query error, and what the application saw
panels.description: Each row is one query in one run, paired with one rule or alert that reads it; a query read by three rules has three rows. Sketch and parameters are the approximate plan the planner chose: the sketch type and its size (for KMV, k is how many hashes it keeps; for HLL, precision p means 2^p registers). Fidelity compares the rule's decisions on the exact and approx answers: an episode is a stretch of consecutive evaluations where the exact rule fires, an incident is an attack or change the data generator injected (synthetic data only). Hover a fidelity cell to read all of it.

properties.value: Defined per application. Threshold alert: evaluations where exact and approx agree on firing. Autoscaler: matched scaling actions over matched, false and missed ones. Rollout controller: rollouts decided the same. Top clients: mean clients shared by the exact and approx top lists, as a fraction of the list size. Rule: entity-evaluations where exact and approx agree on whether the rule is active.

result.text: not run: a query it uses has no approximate plan

panels.description: Dataset: the Data section above describes it. Configuration: the largest relative error the approximate plan may have, whether raw samples are kept so a query can still read them, and whether the planner may pick a plan that cannot promise that error target. Policy: what a rule does when an answer's error bound leaves its check open (plain ignores the bound, bound takes no action, rerun asks the exact plan).
